{{Quote|River of fire. Sand like ground glass. This is not a very pleasant place, Master.|Aayla Secura|<ref name="SW44">[[Star Wars (1998) 44|''Star Wars'' (1998) 44]]</ref>}}
'''Kintan''' was the homeworld of the [[Nikto/Legends|Nikto]]. After a supernova explosion near the [[Star system/Legends|system]], evolution of the Nikto divided into five subspecies. Kintan was located within the [[Si'Klaata Cluster/Legends|Si'Klaata Cluster]], on the [[Ac'fren Spur]].

[[Kintan strider/Legends|Kintan striders]], also found around [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] as pets of Hutts, were originally from Kintan. However, they were driven to extinction on the planet itself.

==History==
In [[26,000 BBY/Legends|26,000 BBY]], the [[Cult of M'dweshuu]] formed on Kintan. This violent cult worshiped the nearby [[M'dweshuu]] supernova. Around [[25,130 BBY]], the Cult came to power, and the planet was plunged into four civil wars. In [[25,100 BBY]], under the terms of the [[Treaty of Vontor]], the Niktos were permanently indentured to the Hutts. The Cult did briefly drive the Hutts offworld about [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]]. Kintan apparently did join the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] at least two decades before the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], having direct [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Senate]] representation, but the Senators were merely mouthpieces for the Niktos' Hutt masters. A new wave of Cult violence broke out in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], making travel on the [[Sisar Run/Legends|Sisar Run]] dangerous.

[[File:BurningMoonRangeAndFireRiverKintan.jpg|thumb|left|180px]]

During the time of the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], a proxy conflict between the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] and [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], [[Miner/Legends|miners]] on the world had discovered [[Cave/Legends|cave]] [[Painting/Legends|paintings]], presumably made by pre-civilized Nikto. Eventually, someone was sent to discover the history behind the paintings. Findings revealed that the paintings depicted four terrible wars in Kintan's ancient past and honored a [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] named [[Da-Shek Yalaa]].<ref name="SWTOR">{{TORcite|type=crewskill|Archaelogy|A Painted History}}</ref>

The [[Morgukai]] warrior tradition arose on the planet, elite and isolated from other Nikto. In [[30 BBY/Legends|30 BBY]], exiled [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Kh'aris Fenn]] took up residence in [[Fortress Kh'aris]] on Kintan, guarded by the last two Morgukai, [[Tsyr]] and [[Bok]]. The two Morgukai kidnapped the Twi'lek heir [[Nat Secura]] and brought him to the fortress, but the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] saved Nat and slew Tsyr. Bok died on [[Saleucami/Legends|Saleucami]] during the [[Outer Rim Sieges/Legends|Outer Rim Sieges]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], along with an army of his clones.

The planet was later [[Subjugation of Kintan|taken over]] by the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] in [[26 ABY/Legends|26 ABY]]. During the occupation, 75% of the Nikto population was either enslaved or killed, while the rest either fled Kintan or went into hiding in the planets most inhospitable areas.<ref name="GatORW" />
